title: Drum solos and the New Orleans bass drum
summary: He says old drummers took breaks, not choruses, and New Orleans drummers used more bass drum and rolls.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: When did drum solos first come in? I noticed, of course, today you have to play drum solos over there at times.
But when did that start, do you think?

Oh, I wouldn't know how that's. Well, the old-time drummers, no, they didn't take a whole solo. I don't remember none of them taking a whole, but they took breaks. Make a break on the ending. In some numbers, them days you might have some numbers called for a four-bar break, a drummer running there. But most of the endings of the drummer are running there. Now, all those men I know used to take plenty of drum solos. I was doing a flash when they were redhead happy when he's worked at the old Lyric, Lyric Theater. He'd take plenty of drum solos. And that was only with Carl Bells. He had one shiny block. No sock stand to do show, but he was very flashy. And Faso was another man. But I asked, like the drummers doing it today, taking chorus, you know, one or two choruses. I don't remember drummers doing that all the time. I don't remember. Because we didn't do it in my time of playing, you know, all the way a chorus all the way through. Maybe some of them did it, but I never see any of them, you know.
People have told me that one of the main things about New Orleans drummers in a dance band, they use a little more bass drum and keep that bass drum moving out.
Did you ever notice out of other drummers from away from here that they don't use as much bass?

They don't, no. I mean, I've seen drummers play it with big bands. They hardly test the band. I've seen guys play this, take their foot and tip their foot pedal, and just keep their beat against the drum. But they'd be playing a whole lot of these cymbals. Yeah, I've seen that. Yeah, but they'd be fast, a whole lot of parallelism on their snare drum. Another thing we were short around, lots of drummers couldn't roll much around here. Roll a snare drum, you see, they couldn't do that. That was no entouphal in time. All the old drummers, mostly, would roll a snare drum.
